newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: New Lithuanian government takes power.
newsitem.headline: New Lithuanian government takes power.

text.p: The new right-wing government of the Baltic state of Lithuania formally took office on Tuesday as its ministers were sworn in and its programme was approved by parliament.

Lithuanian independence leader Vytautas Landsbergis, who spearheaded the small country's fight to quit the former Soviet Union in 1991, led his Homeland Union party to victory over former Communists earlier this month.
The Homeland Union formed a coalition with the Christian Democrats and the government has a comfortable majority with 86 seats in the 141-member parliament.
The government has promised to pursue the country's economic transformation five years after it quit the former Soviet Union and pursue NATO and European Union (EU) membership.
"We have promised to continue reforms, that is why this government was elected," new Finance Minister Rolandas Matiliauskas told Reuters.
The government is led by Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius and Landsbergis has taken the post of parliament speaker. Many expect him to run for the presidency in 1998.
The government's programme, approved with 87 votes for and 21 against, includes pledges to boost the minimum wage and pensions but also tax breaks for companies and a cut in VAT.
One of the new government's key aims is eventually to end the peg of the country's litas currency to the dollar.
